title: Kernel collab lab notes - queue calibration sprint
content:
Meeting: Kernel Collab Lab — Queue Calibration Sprint
Dates: 2026-04-14 (notes) / last updates 2026-04-16
Facilitator: Ava Chen
Attendees: Ava, Ravi, Sofia, Benji, Hannah, plus on-call: Mateo (via Slack)
Purpose: capture progress and outstanding risks for the focused work this sprint: stabilizing queue-calibrator-v2, KV-cache warming heuristics, and a lightweight kernel handshake refactor to reduce head-of-line latency variability.

1) Quick context and goals
- Sprint focus (2 weeks): bring queue-calibrator-v2 to beta behind feature flag, validate warmup heuristics on canary traffic, land kernel-handshake-refactor v1.
- Success criteria for the sprint: end-to-end median p99 tail reductions >= 15% on interactive tests for short sequences (<=64 tokens) without >5% throughput regression on steady-state workloads; 0 known data-loss regressions in KV cache shadow experiments.

2) Kernel updates (Benji)
- Kernel-handshake-refactor v1: landed a minimal refactor that moves the handshake off the hot path and batches handshake ops across conflated requests. Microbenchmarks show ~8% lower allocation spikes under synthetic bursts. PR: linked.
- Observed: a small regression in cold-start time for GPUs that had not been warmed for >30 minutes (p50 cold latency +7%). Hypothesis: refactor changed ordering of preflight probes and deferred a partial allocator warm step.
- Next steps: revert the deferred probe in v1.1 if canary shows same regression (Ravi owner, SRV-2376). Tentative patch by 2026-04-17.

3) Queue calibrator (Sofia)
- queue-calibrator-v2 prototype: implements dynamic bucket sizing based on observed arrival jitter and in-flight kernel occupancy instead of fixed time windows. Live canary running in eu-west-1 on 2 pods.
- Early results (canary traffic, 48h): median latency for short chats down 12%, burst-induced p99 reduced by 18%; however, one class of multi-turn requests (session reuse with KV hot path) saw a small increase in tail errors (0.11% -> 0.22%).
- Root cause analysis: calibration occasionally shrinks a bucket mid-coalescence when a late-arriving high-cost request is observed; this causes reordering and forces kernel to do extra KV swap work.
- Mitigation plan: introduce a short lock window (10ms) after a bucket is formed to absorb late arrivals; this reduces forced reorders. Sofia to ship candidate today (2026-04-16) behind feature flag.

4) KV cache and warming heuristics (Ravi)
- Shadow-warm runs: implemented a passive warming probe that replayed a small subset of recent prefixes to refill KV entries in the shadow cache without impacting production tokens. 3-day run on canary showed 22% reduction in first-token latency for warmable sessions.
- Concern: the current warming probe is too aggressive on high-cardinality traffic (customer X format) — increased memory churn on a dedicated pool. We need a selective filter.
- Action: add a TTL-based filter that demotes sessions with >50 unique prefixes per minute from warm candidates. Ravi to add metric (warm-evict-count) and limit by 2026-04-18.

5) Experiment instrumentation and metrics (Hannah)
- New dashboards: queue-calibrator overview and kv-warm shadow vs prod comparison created in Grafana (links in Confluence). Key metrics added: bucket-size distribution, calibrator-decision-rate, warm-evict-count, kernel-handshake-latency.
- Alert thresholds proposed: calibrator-decision-rate spike (>80% change in 5m) and warm-evict-count > 500/min on a single node. Team agreed to short-term alerts to catch regressions during rollout.

6) Reliability/bugs flagged
- Data-loss risk: two minor cache invalidation races found in shadow run; both cause stale KV reads only in shadow mode but must be fixed before wide rollout. Ticket created SRV-2381 (Benji owner).
- Throughput regression: in one stress test, calibrator + handshake refactor combinatorially increased kernel queue jitter causing CPU steal on co-located processes. Mitigation: throttle calibrator decision CPU budget (soft cap) until improved kernel affinity logic is landed.

7) Action items (owners & ETA)
- Ravi: Patch kernel-handshake-refactor to reintroduce partial preflight probe ordering (v1.1), test on canary. ETA: 2026-04-17. Ticket SRV-2376.
- Sofia: Ship queue-calibrator lock-window (10ms) behind flag, monitor errors. ETA: 2026-04-16.
- Benji: Fix shadow cache invalidation races, add unit tests and a stress harness. ETA: 2026-04-20. Ticket SRV-2381.
- Hannah: Wire alerts into paging for calibrator-decision-rate spikes and add per-customer warm-evict-count visualization. ETA: 2026-04-19.
- Ava: Draft rollout checklist for queue-calibrator-v2 (canary -> staged -> beta) and coordinate with SRE for capacity reservations. ETA: 2026-04-18. Confluence draft linked.

8) Risks and open questions
- Risk: calibrator-induced reorders can amplify KV churn; need robust heuristics to avoid oscillation.
- Open question: should warming probes be stateful per-customer or purely statistical at pool-level? Tradeoff between memory and hit-rate discussed; place on agenda for architecture sync next week.
- Risk: overlapping rollouts (calibrator + handshake + warm heuristics) increase blast radius; recommended to sequence rollouts and keep strict feature flags.

9) Notes from on-call and incident learnings
- On-call (Mateo) noted a recurring pattern of p95 spikes at 03:00 UTC tied to a nightly batch job that bursts ephemeral sessions; plan to add a burst classifier so calibrator treats those as background traffic.
- Incident postmortem from last week (link): improved documentation for kernel failure modes added to runbook.

10) Meeting decisions and cadence
- Decision: proceed with lock-window mitigation and the handshake preflight revert for v1.1 before expanding calibrator to the US region.
- Cadence: kernel collab lab will meet twice weekly (Tue/Thu 30m) for the duration of this sprint; daily async check-ins on the #kernel-collab Slack channel.

Appendix: quick references
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428
- Jira tickets: SRV-2376 (handshake refactor), SRV-2381 (shadow cache invalidation)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/queue-calibrator-design

Freeform notes / TODOs (quick scratchpad)
- Evaluate lowering lock-window if we see throughput drop; try 6ms micro-bench.
- Check kernel affinity scheduler PR for potential CPU steal improvement (Benji to review).
- Confirm warm probe rate-limiter does not bias cache towards large customers.

End of notes.
